description: The plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number and accuracy (ACC) percentage for various models. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" with a logarithmic scale, ranging from 0 to 10^3, and tick labels at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" with a linear scale, ranging from 60 to 80, and tick labels at intervals of 5. The plot displays six lines representing different models: Base (black, solid line, circle markers), FT (blue, solid line, triangle markers), IKE (red, solid line, triangle markers), MEND (brown, dashed line, diamond markers), MEMIT (purple, solid line, triangle markers), and ROME (green, solid line, square markers). The Base line starts at around 60% ACC at a co-occurrence number of 3 and increases to approximately 67% at 3 x 10^3. The FT line begins at around 61% ACC at 3 and rises to about 69% at 3 x 10^3. The IKE line starts at roughly 64% ACC at 3 and reaches around 71% at 3 x 10^3. The MEND line begins at approximately 65.5% ACC at 3 and increases to about 75% at 3 x 10^3. The MEMIT line starts at around 65.5% ACC at 3 and rises to approximately 73.5% at 3 x 10^3. The ROME line begins at roughly 72% ACC at 3 and increases to about 78% at 3 x 10^2 before plateauing at 78% at 3 x 10^3. All lines exhibit an overall increasing trend as the co-occurrence number increases.
